description.value: The SS Naramata is a historic tugboat preserved at the S.S. Sicamous Marine Heritage Park on the Penticton waterfront, alongside the famous SS Sicamous sternwheeler and other Okanagan lake vessels. The park interprets over a century of inland marine transportation history in the Okanagan Valley, with connections to the Kettle Valley Railway era that cycling tourists on the KVR trail will find compelling. It is run by the S.S. Sicamous Marine Heritage Society, a volunteer-driven nonprofit dedicated to education and community outreach.

Sicamous Marine Heritage Park in Penticton; the website at sssicamous.ca confirms it as one of several preserved vessels at the park, with address 1099 Lakeshore Drive West and phone (250) 492-0403 drawn from the contact page. None of the fetched pages mention bike parking, washrooms, water refill, or any other cyclist-specific amenities, so all amenity fields remain null. The site is clearly operational, with an active events calendar, gift shop, and museum programming.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The SS Naramata is a legitimate, active heritage attraction on the Penticton waterfront with strong appeal to touring cyclists exploring the KVR corridor; a listing would benefit visitors looking for cultural stops along the route.
enrichment_extras.notes: The park also preserves the SS Sicamous, CN Tug #6, and references to other Okanagan vessels; if those have separate OSM records, deduplication across the site complex should be reviewed.
